attempts.summary: Configured VyOS (node1) as router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.1.0/24 via eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.2.0/24 via eth2). Applied a default-drop forward filter with established/related accepted and one explicit-allow rule for TCP/5432 from eth1→eth2 (node2→node3). Verified node2 can reach node3:5432 while ping and all other ports/directions between the LANs are rejected. Also opened tcp/5432 in node3's local firewalld (host-level default deny) so the allowed flow actually reaches the service. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state on each, rebooted each node individually, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id, and re-verified config persistence and identical firewall/connectivity behavior after each restart.
